title: Mitigating Lost Updates with Optimistic Concurrency Control
explanation: Optimistic Concurrency Control assumes conflicts are rare. Instead of locking database rows, it allows multiple transactions to read data simultaneously. Each record receives a version number or timestamp. When a transaction attempts to write, the database checks if the stored version matches the read version. If they match, the update succeeds and the version increments. If a concurrent transaction modified the record first, the version check fails. The current transaction rolls back and must retry. This mechanism prevents race conditions in high-throughput APIs without the performance bottlenecks of pessimistic locking. However, high contention causes repeated rollbacks, which degrades throughput.
takeaway: Use optimistic locking for read-heavy systems, but implement exponential backoff on retries to handle high contention gracefully.
author: Muhammad Junaeid
